The panel's dock surface for an ACTIVE document tab. Read at dispatch

members.name: OnDocumentClosed
members.doc:
Called when a document tab of this kind closes. Null = nothing to do.
One kind may fan out to several panels (a .mmodel document feeds both
mesh editors) — that stays inside the panel's own closure.

types.name: FEditorPanelRegistry
types.doc:
Find hands out a pointer INTO the storage and the callers dispatch through
it — `desc->OnDocumentClosed(path)`, `desc->GetSurface()`. A vector made
that pointer a liability twice over: a registration after the pointer was
taken reallocated and left it dangling (a plugin registering its panels the
first time a document of its kind closes is exactly that shape), and
replacing a descriptor in place destroyed the very std::function running
through the old pointer. So descriptors live in a deque — push_back never
moves the elements already handed out — and a re-registration retires the
old entry instead of overwriting it, which keeps every pointer Find ever
returned readable for the life of the registry. Retired entries are bounded
by the number of re-registrations and never freed on purpose.

types.name: FEditorDockPanelInstance
types.doc:
One live dock-panel instance. The surface is what the tab hosts; the hooks
are what the shell needs to keep an instance the engine does not own as a
member alive and answerable — a Tick nothing else calls for it, and the
state it must carry across a restart.

types.name: FEditorDockPanelDesc
types.doc:
A dock panel that can exist more than once. Separate from
FEditorPanelDesc above, which describes an asset-editor DOCUMENT kind:
this one describes a docked tool panel and the shape the audit's R9 asked
for — a declared ceiling and a factory, instead of one by-value member
reached through a hardcoded id.

members.name: Kind
members.doc:
Tab kind, e.g. "ContentBrowser". Instance 0 is spelled exactly this;
extras are "<Kind>#<n>".

members.name: Title
members.doc: Base title. Extras append their 1-based instance number.

members.name: Icon
members.doc: Lucide glyph for the Window menu row.

members.name: Neighbour
members.doc:
Tab an extra instance docks beside when the layout has no home for it.
Empty = the kind itself.

members.name: MaxInstances
members.doc:
1 = the singleton every dock panel used to be, and the Window menu
never offers a second one. A kind raises this only once a second
instance is genuinely driven end to end — a tab that exists but is
never ticked or never rendered is worse than no command at all.

members.name: CreatesPrimary
members.doc:
Instance 0 comes from Create as well. True for every panel a plugin
registers — the shell has no member for it, so without this the kind
could only ever have had "extra" instances of a first one that never
exists. The editor's own dock panels build instance 0 as a shell member
and set it false.

types.name: FEditorDockPanelRegistry
types.doc:
Same stable-address contract as the registry above: Find hands out a
pointer into the storage and callers dispatch through it, so descriptors
live in a deque and a re-registration retires the old entry rather than
destroying a std::function that may be running.

The instance is defined in the EditorFramework library. It used to be a
function-local static in this header, which is one instance per image that
includes it: a plugin DLL would have registered into its own copy and the
editor would never have seen the panel.

members.name: Unregister
members.doc:
A plugin calls this from its ShutdownModule. The factory is code inside
the plugin's DLL, so it has to be destroyed while that DLL is still
mapped — a std::function destroyed after the unload calls into freed
pages. The entry itself is retired, not erased, so a pointer Find handed
out earlier stays readable; its Create is simply empty.

Live panels go first, through the handler the editor installs: their
widgets, and the shared-pointer control blocks that own them, were
allocated by the plugin's code too.

members.name: SetUnregisterHandler
members.doc:
Installed by the editor: closes and releases every live instance of a
kind that is about to be unregistered.

members.name: Revision
members.doc:
Bumped by every registration, so a menu built from All() can tell that a
plugin enabled after startup added a panel it does not list yet.

types.name: FMcpPathPolicy
types.doc:
Where a tool may touch the disk. A path an agent sends is resolved against
the project root and must stay inside it after `..` is folded AND after
every symlink or junction on the way is followed; a network path is refused
before anything resolves it, since merely opening \\host\share hands that
host the user's NTLM hash. `extensions` (lower-case, with the dot) limits
what the file may be, so a screenshot cannot overwrite an INI or the
preferences that hold the access level; empty allows any.
